content.text:
I found nothing to flag: every factual claim in the document is backed by the record. There's no went_wrong field, so nothing had to be checked for where it sits. I left out the action items and the "had it been otherwise" what-ifs, since neither is judged.

The one call worth a second look is the root cause. It says, without a hedge, that the code the flag turns on raised the error. The error itself is logged (G5309). The tie to the flag rests on timing: the flag change at 21:33:31 (P1), the evaluation logs going from off to split to on (G7e5d, G971b, Gce95), and the errors starting in that same minute. I counted that as supported. Elsewhere the document says the trigger is suspected, not confirmed, as the record asked.

supported.quote: The spend-summary code that monthly-spend-feature turns on raises a ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 for some account page requests, and those requests fail with that error.
The evidence does not show why the divisor is zero for those requests.
Switching on a new monthly-spending feature sent account pages through new code that divided by zero for some shoppers, so their account pages failed.
If anyone switches monthly-spend-feature back on before the spend-summary code is fixed, account pages could fail the same way again.
Shoppers' account pages failed to load
The requests failed with a ZeroDivisionError raised at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, starting in the minute the incident began.
Before that minute, the only account-page failures logged were shoppers closing the connection.
That code ran because admin switched the monthly-spend-feature flag on at {P1.1}.
The flag read off on every evaluation before that minute, was split between off and on during that minute, and read on for every evaluation after it.

A deploy or a revision change: no deploy came back from the window that was read, the flag change was the only production change read back, and account pages rendered normally with the running revision in place before the onset.
A different flag change: the flag provider's history showed only this one flag change by anyone other than Argus in the hour that was read.
Shoppers closing their connections: these errors were logged while the service ran normally before the onset, and stopped being logged before it.
The code path behind the flag divides by a value that is zero for some account page requests, and those requests fail with the resulting error.
The flag was switched from off for all traffic to on for all traffic within a single minute. No staged rollout, and no automatic check of the error rate tied to the flag change, was seen.
No test or pre-enablement check was seen that ran the spend-summary path with the flag on against account data that gives a zero divisor.
No handling was seen that keeps an error in the spend-summary section from failing the whole account page.
